title: Maha Mrityunjaya Mantra
summary: Also known as the Rudra Mantra or Tryambakam Mantra, this powerful verse from the Rig Veda (7.59.12) is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is believed to promote healing, longevity, and liberation from the cycle of death and rebirth.

verses.sanskrit:
ॐ त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् |
उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय माऽमृतात् ||
verses.translation: We worship the three-eyed Lord Shiva, who is fragrant and who nourishes and nurtures all beings. As the ripe cucumber is freed from its bondage to the vine, may He liberate us from death for the sake of immortality.
verses.transliteration:
oṃ tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭi-vardhanam
urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya mā 'mṛtāt
verses.meaning: Om - the primordial sound; Tryambakam - the three-eyed one (Shiva); Yajāmahe - we worship; Sugandhim - fragrant, sweet-smelling; Puṣṭi-vardhanam - one who nourishes and increases prosperity; Urvārukam - cucumber/melon; Iva - like; Bandhanāt - from bondage/attachment; Mṛtyoḥ - from death; Mukṣīya - may I be liberated; Mā - not; Amṛtāt - from immortality/liberation

verses.sanskrit:
ॐ हौं जूं सः |
ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः |
ॐ त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम् |
उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान्मृत्योर्मुक्षीय माऽमृतात् |
ॐ स्वः भुवः भूः ॐ |
सः जूं हौं ॐ ||
verses.translation: Extended version with bija mantras: Om Haum Jum Sah. Om Bhur Bhuvah Svah. We worship the three-eyed one who is fragrant and who nourishes all. Like a ripe cucumber freed from its stem, may we be liberated from death, not from immortality. Om Svah Bhuvah Bhuh Om. Sah Jum Haum Om.
verses.transliteration:
oṃ hauṃ jūṃ saḥ
oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ
oṃ tryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭi-vardhanam
urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya mā 'mṛtāt
oṃ svaḥ bhuvaḥ bhūḥ oṃ
saḥ jūṃ hauṃ oṃ
verses.meaning: This extended version includes the bija (seed) mantras and the Vyahriti (Bhur Bhuvah Svah - the three planes of existence). The bija mantras Haum, Jum, and Sah are powerful sound vibrations that enhance the mantra's potency. The reverse order at the end (Svah Bhuvah Bhuh) represents the return journey from higher consciousness back to earthly awareness.

verses.translation: Om, salutations to Shiva. This is often chanted after the Maha Mrityunjaya Mantra as a closing invocation.
verses.meaning: Om - the primordial sound; Namaḥ - salutations, bow to; Śivāya - to Shiva (the auspicious one). This five-syllable mantra (Panchakshari) is one of the most important mantras in Shaivism, representing the five elements and the five actions of Shiva.
